components.comparisonReason: Shows one framed marketing capture from the capture pipeline at its exact framed pixel size, with a device-sized width, tilt and bleed. It is not a general remote image: no fallback, loading hook or decode sizing (catch.network_image), no hero assembly or readability overlay (catch.detail_media), and never graded, because captures must keep their rendered pixels (catch.graded_image). It composes catch.text for its caption rather than implementing text.
components.notes: Website T4 under D18: @catch/web-ui draws a device-framed app capture with its caption, optionally sized (sm 280, md 330, lg 380 or fill), turned (tilt) or bleeding off its band (bleed, proposal L3); website/src/shared/media/captureSlot.ts resolves a tool/marketing/capture_manifest.json slot id to its props. Search aliases: AppScreenshot, AppCapture, DeviceFrame, PhoneFrame, PhoneMockup, ScreenshotFrame.

Pure geometry and the server-side SVG live in activityArtwork.ts (@catch/web-ui/artwork); activityArtworkParity.test.ts pins both to the Flutter painter. Search aliases: ActivityCover, ActivityArtwork, EventCover, FallbackImage, PatternCover.

Website T4 under D18. Twin of the Flutter member catch.event_card.thumbnail (Flutter EventThumbnail): the event's uploaded photo, or EventBackdropImage when there is none or it fails to load. Never a stand-in photo. Search aliases: EventImage, EventMedia, EventPhoto, PosterImage.

Website T4 under D18 (G7 typographic organiser cover). Twin of the Flutter member catch.organizer_poster.artwork (Flutter OrganizerPlaceholderCover): the organiser's name and city over its activity artwork, initials when compact; deterministic per organiser. The Flutter artwork does not set type yet; converging it on this recipe is a follow-up. Search aliases: OrganizerCover, OrganiserCover, TypographicCover, OrganizerFallback, Monogram.

Website T4 under D18. Same symbol as Flutter OrganizerCover (catch.club_cover); becomes its react record when that registry is free: the organiser's photo, or OrganizerPlaceholderCover when there is none or it fails to load. Never a stand-in photo or a grey box. Flutter binds a Club; the website binds the public listing's name, city and activity. Search aliases: OrganizerCover, OrganizerImage, OrganizerImage.

components.comparisonReason: A full-width section of a web page, which CatchSurface does not draw today. The redesign folds it into Surface block band when its first redesigned consumer lands.
components.notes: Website T4 under D18 (CAT-248). A full-width Website v2 section on the white, paper, ink or an accent ground from the CAT-245 palette tokens; it remaps the theme ink roles to the ground's inks, resolves the ink ground through the dark theme, sets the 112/64/32px section rhythm, and declares the catch-page container that CatchSplit, CatchGrid, CatchScroller and CatchScrollStory query for their phone arrangement below 840px. Search aliases: PageSection, Section, SectionBand, ColorBand, ColourBlock, GroundSection, FullBleedSection, Stripe.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-248). Two columns at 1:1, 7:5, or a 380px (booking) or 420px (organiser) rail on either side; they stack in source order when the page is narrower than 840px, snapped from the boards' 900px to the expanded window size. Search aliases: TwoColumn, TwoColumns, Columns, SplitLayout, SideBySide, Sidebar, SidebarLayout, RailLayout.
components.comparisonReason: A Website v2 section that places media beside copy inside a band; CatchPaneLayout arranges sibling workspace panes of an app screen.

components.notes: Website T4 under D18 (CAT-248). Two, three or four equal columns, one or two on a page narrower than 840px, spaced with a CatchGaps role; as ul or ol it wraps each child in a list item. Search aliases: GridLayout, ResponsiveGrid, TileGrid, CardGrid, Columns, MasonryGrid.
components.comparisonReason: Equal columns whose count follows the page's catch-page container, wrapping into further rows; catch.stack lays children in one column or one row sized by their content. Deprecated: P7 replaces it with CatchStack direction=row equal collapseBelow, after which it is deleted rather than registered as a stack.

A full-bleed band row: its first item lines up with the page content edge while items scroll out to the viewport edge, it never wraps, and its items can grow to share the row (the boards' format tiles). catch.rail is a content-width row that fades the edge hiding more and wraps into a grid on desktops. The two overlap; folding page-edge bleed into CatchRail and retiring CatchScroller is a follow-up.
components.notes: Website T4 under D18 (CAT-248). A keyboard-focusable sideways rail whose items snap to its start; a page-edge rail pads its first item to the content edge of a full-width CatchBand while items scroll to the viewport edge. Search aliases: Carousel, HorizontalScroll, Rail, Slider, ScrollRow, Shelf, HorizontalList, Swiper.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-248). Pinned media beside chapters: the chapter crossing the viewport's middle becomes active, arrows step through chapters with a polite position announcement, inactive chapters recede to the ground's secondary ink (AA), and below 840px the media and controls pin to the top of the band. Search aliases: ScrollytellingSection, StickyStory, PinnedMedia, Walkthrough, StepThrough, FeatureTour, Chapters.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-249). A calendar date on a palette ground: weekday, a displayS day and month in one time element, 72 x 78px and 56 x 66px on a phone. Search aliases: DateBadge, CalendarTile, DateBlock, DateChip, EventDate, CalendarIcon.

components.comparisonReason: A website T4 layout that places one booking card beside the page, or behind a docked bar that opens it in a sheet. It composes CatchDock, CatchSheet and CatchButton and implements none of their contracts.
components.notes: Website T4 under D18 (CAT-248). The event page's booking card: a sticky aside beside the content on desktop, and on phones a docked bar (CatchDock) whose action opens the same card in a CatchSheet. It switches on the page's container width (catch-page below 840px), not the viewport. Search aliases: StickySidebar, BookingAside, StickyCard, BookingPanel, MobileBookingBar.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-249): the FAQ list on the home and host pages, on native details and summary. One answer is open at a time by default (the name attribute), with a plus that turns to a minus, a hairline between questions and the question in titleL. Website-only: the app draws no FAQ. Search aliases: FAQ, Disclosure, Collapsible, ExpandableList, QuestionList.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-249). A label, its value and an optional note on a ground: the event page facts (When, Where, Price) and, as a stat on the displayS step, the owner view numbers with a positive change note. Nearest concept: catch.metric_strip (CatchMetricSection and CatchMetricTile), which sets the value above its label in the mono or metric role; the v2 tile leads with the label, so it is not a CatchMetricTile recipe. Search aliases: MetricTile, StatTile, StatCard, FactCard, KpiTile, InfoTile, KeyFact.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-249). One pill split into ground-coloured segments by share, with a legend that reads each segment and its formatted share; the bar itself is hidden from assistive technology. The owner view uses it for visitor sources. Nearest concept: catch.mini_bar_chart (CatchBarIndicator), one vertical bar against a maximum; a share bar divides one whole, so it is not a CatchBarIndicator recipe. Search aliases: StackedBar, ProportionBar, SplitBar, PercentBar, SourceBreakdown, ShareChart.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-251). The organiser page's identity: a cover photo or ground, an 88px monogram over its foot, the name with an optional verified seal, a tag, the headline, a meta line, a stats line and the caller's actions. Search aliases: ProfileHero, OrganiserHeader, OrganizerHeader, IdentityHeader, BioHeader.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-251). A rounded card on one Website v2 ground that holds what the page arranges in it: the share card, a form step, the claim pitch and its points. Library text inside takes the ground's inks, ink resolves through the dark theme, and an outlined card draws the emphasis stroke in its ground's ink at opacity.groundCardOutline (the boards' white cards). Field contract: a CatchField in the card draws the boards' boxed input at rest (a white fill and the emphasis stroke at field.restLineAlpha; a field.restTintOnDarkAlpha tint on ink) through --catch-field-rest-*; outside a card a field stays the quiet row. Nearest concept: catch.surface (CatchSurface), whose tones are theme surfaces, not palette grounds. Search aliases: GroundPanel, ColorCard, PitchCard, TintCard, Callout.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-249). One link in an organiser's link-in-bio list: an optional icon tile, title, subtitle, an optional owner stats line and an outward arrow; a pinned link takes an accent ground. A new-tab link carries rel noopener and a screen-reader note. Search aliases: LinkButton, LinkCard, LinkRow, BioLink, LinkInBio, LinkItem, LinktreeLink.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-249). An average rating in the displayXxl step over its star distribution: one coral bar per star count, scaled to the largest row and read by the caller's row label, with an optional policy note. Search aliases: RatingBreakdown, RatingHistogram, ReviewSummary, ScoreSummary, StarDistribution, RatingBars.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-249). One review as an article named by the reviewer: stars, a verification badge slot (Booked on Catch or Unverified), the text, the organiser's reply and a footer slot for Reply. The row recipe is the organiser page's hairline list; the card recipe is the event page's paper card. Search aliases: Review, ReviewCard, ReviewRow, Testimonial, CustomerReview, Comment.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-249). Five native radios drawn as stars in 44px targets, so arrow keys choose; stars fill to the hovered or chosen value. Named by visible text or a label. Search aliases: RatingInput, StarPicker, RatingPicker, StarSelector, RateControl.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-249). A read-only rating out of five in coral deep, read as one image with the caller's label; values round to whole stars. Search aliases: Stars, StarDisplay, RatingStars, StarScore, Rating.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-249). A past moment: a graded photo under the detail-hero scrim (CatchHeroImage, the catch.detail_media twin) with white copy, or a ground when there is no photo, with an optional displayXl figure, a title and a caption at its foot. 220px tall, 170px below 840px. Nearest concept: catch.organizer_poster (CatchPoster), whose photo layout carries a kicker and a display title over the media; the v2 tile leads with a figure and a small title, so it is not a CatchPoster recipe. Search aliases: MomentTile, PhotoCard, StatTile, MediaTile, GalleryTile, HighlightTile.
components.comparisonReason: A past-moment or hamper photo tile: it draws its photo through CatchHeroImage (catch.detail_media) and its figure, title and caption through CatchLegacyText (catch.text), and both of those still render on their own elsewhere. It adds the fixed tile height, the ground fallback and the figure layout, so it is neither the detail hero nor a text style. Its figure is marketing copy, not a caller-formatted metric with missing-data states (catch.analytics_metric); it shows no icon (catch.icon_tile) and is not a choice target (catch.option_card); its ground is a fixed v2 palette fill for a photo-less tile, not one of the catch.surface roles that tell children what they sit on.

components.notes: Website T4 under D18 (CAT-249). One link on a ground: a status-role label, a displayXs title and a meta line held to the foot, at least 150px tall (sized to its copy below 840px). The event page uses it for "More from" the organiser; the organiser page's "Next up" card is its feature size on ink, with a tag, a detail line and an action label (CAT-251). Nearest concepts: catch.event_card (EventCard, the app ticket with an activity backdrop and clock) and catch.organizer_poster (CatchPoster); the v2 card has no media, so it is neither. Search aliases: EventCard, EventTile, MoreCard, TeaserCard, SummaryCard, LinkCard.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-252). An event without a photo, set in type on a ground: the kicker and date on the top line, a displayXxl title and the place at the foot, in CatchHeroImage's framed geometry (16:10 at radius lg, 4:3 below 840px). It repeats the page's own words, so it is hidden from screen readers. Nearest concepts: catch.detail_media (CatchHeroImage, whose fallback is a branded gradient without words) and catch.organizer_poster (CatchPoster, organiser material with media). Search aliases: EventPoster, PosterCover, TypePoster, NoPhotoCover.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-249). A scannable QR code drawn as one SVG path, ink on white in every theme, with a two-module quiet zone; it encodes the value's UTF-8 bytes with qrcode-generator (MIT) and never draws a module under 3px, growing past its size for long links. Search aliases: QRCode, QR, Barcode, ScanCode, ShareCode.

components.comparisonReason: Shows the official App Store or Google Play badge artwork as a link, or a pending button that records the tap. The badge must appear exactly as Apple and Google supply it (no recolour, label or redraw), so it cannot be a catch.button, which draws its own labelled control; it only shares the D20 heights.
components.notes: Website T4 under D18 (CAT-249), proposal L8. A link to the Catch app in the App Store or Google Play drawn with the store's official badge artwork (Apple's black SVG, Google's cropped PNG; Apple's and Google's guidelines forbid a drawn button), never recoloured, stretched or overlaid, at the D20 large (48px) or medium (40px) height. The site hosts the files (website/public/assets/store-badges, with provenance); a store that is not live yet draws the same badge as a button that records the press. Search aliases: AppStoreBadge, AppStoreButton, GooglePlayBadge, DownloadButton, StoreBadge, GetTheApp.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-260). The Website v2 site header: the wordmark, the main links and the page's own controls (a city picker, Get the app) on one 84px row at the content width. Links not marked compact and the wide actions leave the bar below 840px; the footer carries every link. Nearest concept: shared_public_site_header (PublicSiteChrome), the legacy chrome it replaces. Since the one-header change (Explore and the city pages moved to PublicSiteHeader) no route renders it; retire it with its story and test. Search aliases: SiteHeader, TopBar, NavBar, Masthead, PageHeader.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-260). The Website v2 site footer on the ink ground: four titled link columns (two below 840px), each link with an optional quiet note such as 'soon', then the wordmark and tagline over a hairline. Nearest concept: shared_public_site_footer (PublicSiteChrome), the legacy chrome it replaces. Search aliases: SiteFooter, Footer, FooterLinks, Colophon.
components.comparisonReason: Renders CatchText for its own copy; it is a Website v2 page part with its own layout, not a text style, so it uses catch.text rather than implementing it.

Draws a generic phone, tablet or browser-window bezel in CSS around one screen (proposal W1, L9). It lays out no panes: catch.pane_layout arranges workspace screens' list, detail and side panes, while this frame decorates a single picture.
components.notes: Website T4 under D18 (CAT-260). A generic device bezel (phone, Android phone with a punch-hole camera, or tablet held either way; nothing unique to Apple hardware) around an app screen for showing the Catch apps on the website, upright or turned. Geometry is one spec per kind as shares of the frame, so proportions hold at any size. The frame is decoration; the screen image carries the description. A browser kind (proposal W1) puts a quiet window with an optional address around a desktop capture, and bleed (L3) runs a device off its band's bottom edge, which clips it. Nearest concept: CatchAppCaptureImage, which frames a capture as a figure without hardware. Search aliases: BrowserFrame, BrowserWindow, PhoneFrame, DeviceMockup, Bezel, TabletFrame, ScreenFrame.

components.comparisonReason: A website comparison table of event formats against the properties Catch tracks for each, with a format picker. It renders catch.chip for that picker; it does not implement the chip contract.
components.notes: Website host landing, proposal WebFormatMatrix ("Built for every kind of night"). Several event formats' properties side by side: a table on a wide band whose column headings choose a format (its column tinted in the format's colour), and on a phone-width band format chips over the selected format's properties. The selection is shared with the page's night scene. Nearest concept: CatchTable, which lists records rather than comparing formats. Search aliases: WebFormatMatrix, ComparisonTable, FormatComparison, FeatureMatrix.

components.comparisonReason: A pinned, scroll-driven timeline of one evening for the host landing (proposal WebNightScene). On a phone it renders catch.chip for the format picker; it does not implement the chip contract.
components.notes: Website host landing, proposal WebNightScene (a scene mode for the scroll story). One evening, moment by moment, in a single pinned viewport: the scene pins while the reader scrolls a track one step taller per moment; the focused moment's screen fades in on a generic phone and a badge names the event property it relies on. Wide: timeline left, phone right, each moment a button that scrolls to it. Phone width: chips, phone, progress segments and a live caption. Nearest concept: CatchScrollStory, whose chapters scroll beside pinned media. Search aliases: WebNightScene, ScrollScene, PinnedTimeline, OnTheNight.

components.comparisonReason: A website board showing applicants moving from interested to expected. It renders catch.person_avatar for each person and catch.button for the board's demo actions; it implements neither contract.
components.notes: Website host landing, proposal WebPipelineBoard ("From interested to expected"). Numbered step tabs over a board of columns; each guest is a chip that slides into the furthest column it reaches so far. Plays on its own while on screen (not under reduced motion); a chosen tab stops it, replay starts again. Nearest concept: CatchSection columns. Search aliases: WebPipelineBoard, Kanban, BookingFunnel, ApplicantBoard.

components.comparisonReason: A website diagram of how Catch's layers stack for one way of hosting. It renders catch.icon for each layer's glyph; it does not implement the icon contract.
components.notes: Website host landing, proposal WebLayerMap, on the indigo band (L2). Which jobs Catch runs at a chosen layer of adoption: solid white cards for the jobs Catch runs (new ones marked), dashed outlines with what the host keeps for the rest. Paired with a CatchPageTabBar. Nearest concept: CatchTable. Search aliases: WebLayerMap, AdoptionLayers, WaysToUse, FeatureLayers.

components.comparisonReason: A website hero picture: a tilted framed capture on a coloured ground with floating stickers. It composes catch.text for the sticker labels; it does not implement text.
components.notes: Website T4 under D18 (CAT-260). The homepage hero art: a rounded panel on one ground with the app in a device frame and up to three decorative plan stickers, which are hidden from assistive technology and leave pages narrower than 840px. Nearest concept: CatchHeroImage, a photo hero without a device. Search aliases: HeroArt, PhoneShowcase, HeroPanel, FloatingChips.

components.comparisonReason: A website card for one event format: photo or format artwork, the format name and this week's count, as a link or a pressed toggle that filters the week. Not a block that tells children their ground (catch.surface), not a caller-formatted metric with missing-data states (catch.analytics_metric), not an icon-only tile (catch.icon_tile) and not a checked form choice (catch.option_card). It composes catch.text for its labels.
components.notes: Website T4 under D18 (CAT-260). One activity format on its accent: a count line, the format's name and line, and a plan photo at its foot when there is one. It is a pressed toggle when it filters and a link when it navigates. Nearest concept: catch.chip.field (CatchChip choice), the compact filter it pairs with. Search aliases: FormatCard, CategoryTile, ActivityTile, FilterTile.

Website T4 under D18 (CAT-260). One plan as a single link: the photo or a poster on its format accent, a label coloured by its format, the title, host and place, then the price and places left. Below 840px it becomes a row with the media at its start. Nearest concept: shared_preview_card (CatchPreviewCard), which has no media. Search aliases: EventCard, PlanTile, ListingCard, EventPreview.
components.comparisonReason: Renders CatchText for its own copy; it is a Website v2 page part with its own layout, not a text style, so it uses catch.text rather than implementing it.

components.notes: Website T4 under D18 (CAT-260). An organiser on paper: monogram, name (linked when the organiser has a page), what they run, the next plan, and a footnote across from the page's action (Follow, a claim link). Nearest concept: catch.organizer_poster, the photo-led organiser card. Search aliases: HostCard, OrganiserCard, OrganizerCard, FollowCard.
components.comparisonReason: An organiser on paper (monogram, name, what they run, the next plan, a follow action), not one event: it shows no date, venue or booking state, which catch.event_card owns.

components.notes: The library's disclosure list (#948): the homepage FAQ, one question open at a time. Search aliases: FAQ, Disclosure, Collapsible, Expander.
The library's catch.chip twin, rendered on the website through CatchChoiceInput's filter chips.

Implements catch.chip.field: the library's choice group (Flutter's CatchChoiceInput), which arranges CatchChip filter chips, CatchChoiceTile described choices and a CatchText legend. The homepage's format filter, Explore's view, format and date choices and the guest ID page's kind of ID.
Explore's search box for plans and organisers, with its clear button.
/account/ (P4.8a, #1115): the signed-in guest's account, in a private noindex shell; signed out it offers the sign-in sheet.
The account page's tabs (Plans with passes, Following, Reviews, Details, Messages, Privacy and data) drawn from the system; empty states per tab.

/host/billing/: the organiser owner's billing on the web (trial, plan with prices, bills to pay, tools-only buy or cancel); private and noindex; signed out it offers the sign-in sheet. The native Host app shows status only (App Store 3.1.3(f)).
The billing page drawn from the system: trial tile, plan tile with Catch's prices and the tools-only actions, and the bills list with each invoice's Pay action.
The one sign-in sheet: phone code first, then Google and an email link. Opens from the header and inline at the moment of need, never as a gate before browsing.
A button that opens the sign-in sheet and reports the signed-in user.

The header's account entry, provided to the public header: "Sign in" opens the sign-in sheet and a signed-in reader gets "Account". Wide pages draw it as the last item of the top bar's left group; under 600px it joins the phone menu. One state and one sheet serve both, and Firebase loads only for a reader this device has seen signed in or one returning from an email link.
An inline sign-in line at the moment of need (the organiser review form) that opens the sign-in sheet.
